root_cause.text: In `drivers/nfc/pn533/uart.c`, `pn532_receive_buf()` allocated the next `recv_skb` only after consuming and possibly completing a frame, so an `alloc_skb()` failure left the serdev receive callback with an incorrect byte-count return of 0 and a NULL `recv_skb`, violating the `receive_buf()` accounting contract and enabling a later NULL dereference in `skb_put_u8()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `alloc_skb(PN532_UART_SKB_BUFF_LEN, GFP_KERNEL)` to the top of the loop “before consuming the next byte,” returns `i` on allocation failure instead of `0`, and changes the post-frame path from allocating a new skb to `dev->recv_skb = NULL`, matching the commit text that says the old code “already hand[ed] a complete frame to pn533_recv_frame() before allocating a fresh receive buffer” and that failure “can also lead to a NULL dereference on the next skb_put_u8()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allocate the receive skb on demand in pn532_receive_buf() to avoid processing with a missing buffer.
intent_record.what: Inside pn532_receive_buf(), before each byte is processed in the receive loop, a new check was added to allocate dev->recv_skb with alloc_skb(PN532_UART_SKB_BUFF_LEN, GFP_KERNEL) when it is NULL; if allocation fails, the function returns the current loop index i immediately.
intent_record.how: This ensures the UART receive path always has an skb buffer available before appending incoming data, preventing a null dereference or loss of received bytes when the buffer has not yet been initialized; on allocation failure, it stops processing and reports how many bytes were consumed so far.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop reallocating the receive skb immediately after frame processing and clear the pointer instead to avoid receive-path allocation failure.
intent_record.what: The code no longer allocates a new receive skb after calling pn533_recv_frame(); instead of assigning the result of alloc_skb() to dev->recv_skb and returning 0 on allocation failure, it now simply sets dev->recv_skb to NULL.
intent_record.how: After a frame is received and handed off, the driver now clears the receive buffer pointer rather than immediately allocating a replacement buffer. This avoids the possibility of failing the receive path due to an allocation failure at that point, and leaves buffer reallocation to occur elsewhere or on demand.

In `pn532_receive_buf()` the code appends each byte with `skb_put_u8(dev->recv_skb, *data++);` and only after a complete frame is detected does it allocate the next buffer: `pn533_recv_frame(dev->priv, dev->recv_skb, 0); dev->recv_skb = alloc_skb(PN532_UART_SKB_BUFF_LEN, GFP_KERNEL); if (!dev->recv_skb) return 0;`. This matches the vulnerable pattern described: allocation happens after consuming/completing a frame, and on allocation failure the callback returns `0` while `dev->recv_skb` becomes NULL. There is no pre-allocation or error handling to preserve the receive accounting contract before continuing, so the fix is not present here.
